settings.title: Basic hand tools
settings.description: A hacksaw, files, sandpaper, a measuring tape — no power tools. Everything else is in the kit.

settings.title: A bit of space
settings.description: A sturdy table around 1200 × 600 mm and a spot the frame can sit undisturbed while joints cure.

settings.title: A few weekends
settings.description: 25–35 hours across multiple sessions. No rush — bamboo is forgiving and most mistakes are fixable.

settings.title: Set the geometry
settings.description: Lock fat-tyre geometry on the jig — huge clearance for 4-inch-plus tyres at low pressure.

settings.title: Join & wrap
settings.description: Bond the tubes with epoxy and wrap each joint with carbon-fibre tow.

settings.title: Cure
settings.description: Leave it for a full cure — that's where maximum joint strength comes from.

settings.title: Sand, seal & ride
settings.description: Sand smooth, seal the bamboo, fit the headset and bottom bracket. Adventure awaits.

settings.quote: It's very smooth, and it has some kind of suspension due to the very low tyre pressure of 0.5 bar.

settings.question: What tyre sizes will it fit?
settings.answer: Designed for 26×4" or 27.5×4" fat tyres, with massive clearance for sand, snow and soft ground. (Confirm the exact maximum tyre width / fork clearance with us before you order — see flag.)

settings.question: What terrain is a fatbike actually for?
settings.answer: Soft, loose and slippery ground — dry sand, packed snow, mud, beach and bog. The very wide tyres run at low pressure so your weight spreads out and floats over the surface instead of sinking into it. They're also a confidence-inspiring, forgiving ride on normal trails.

settings.question: Is a bamboo frame strong enough for expeditions and a loaded bike?
settings.answer: Very strong for its weight. Bamboo is a light, hollow natural composite and every joint is reinforced with carbon-fibre, giving a high strength-to-weight ratio. Our bamboo is independently tested at Swansea University. Builders ride these frames daily and tour continents — with proper care they last for years.

settings.question: Will it survive cold, wet, sand and salt?
settings.answer: Finished frames are sealed with epoxy resin, so they shrug off cold and wet. After beach or salt rides, rinse off sand and salt, dry the bike, and store it indoors — do that and and with proper care it'll give you years of riding.

settings.question: What gearing and components does it take?
settings.answer: The frame is the frame — you add fork, fat-specific wheels, drivetrain, bars and finishing kit (a fat-tyre fork and wide rims are the parts to get right). Source them from any bike shop, or take a matched component pack from us and we'll advise on fat-specific spec.
